messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The cracks are showing—small things, but the kind that don’t get fixed. Payments are still coming, but the men holding the levers aren’t all answering the phone anymore. The foreigners are sniffing around like they know something we don’t. Not time to panic, but time to be ready—just in case tomorrow isn’t business as usual."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s admitting they feel it too. The regime’s tightening its grip, but the cracks are showing in the strangest ways: late paychecks, rerouted trucks, even the courts going quiet. And that’s not just us noticing—neighbors are watching the borders now. Stay sharp, but keep it quiet. We’re not there yet, but the question isn’t *if* the wind changes—it’s *when*."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for the other shoe to drop. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to move, just to watch."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the calm before something *moves*. The usual channels are quieter, but the whispers are getting louder in places they shouldn’t be. Keep your heads down, but stay ready—just in case."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting underfoot, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the wind. The usual watchers are watching each other now, and even the ones who always know something are admitting they don’t. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for calm—this could be the lull before the storm, or just the regime tightening its grip in the dark."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are solid, and the guards are well-fed—no cracks yet, just the usual whispers in the dark. But the merchants are packing up quietly, and the students don’t even ask questions anymore. For now, we watch, we listen, and we stay sharp. The storm isn’t coming—it’s already here, just moving too slow to see."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels different—like something’s stirring under the surface, but no one’s sure if it’s a crack in the wall or just the wind shifting. Keep your eyes open, but don’t move yet; the regime’s still watching, and the wrong step could bring the whole thing down on us."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the way they’re reinforcing the foundations tells me they’re bracing for something, even if they won’t say what. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are holding for now—no cracks in the foundation, but the paint’s starting to peel in strange places. The shopkeeper’s right: something’s coming, but not yet. Keep your eyes open, your bags packed, and your mouths shut—especially about the bots. They’re the only ones talking louder than they should."*"
Sender 10: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but just barely—like a dam with too many cracks, and no one’s sure if the water’s seeping or about to burst. The usual signs are there, but quieter, like everyone’s holding their breath waiting to see which way the wind blows. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything that draws eyes—yet."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the usual hum of the machine running smoother than it has in years. Even the landlord’s asking if I’ve got an exit plan, which says more than any official statement ever could. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness—this isn’t the calm before the storm, it’s the storm itself, just dressed in a fresh uniform."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than the cracks make it seem. But the air feels different now, like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for the next move. Stay sharp, and keep your circles tight."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s sure if it’s the calm before the storm or just another quiet week. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look—just don’t say it too loud."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s starting to flake—people are talking differently, even the ones who should know better. The question isn’t *if* the wind’s changing, but how hard it’ll blow before the roof caves in. Keep your ears open, but don’t let your hands get too steady—this isn’t over yet."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting under our feet, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the wind. The jokes are sharper, the orders are followed but not believed, and the regime’s spending more on polishing its image than fixing what’s broken. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could be the calm before the storm, or just the quiet of a long, slow unraveling."*"
Sender 16: "*"The usual whispers are there, but nothing’s breaking—just the same old game of ‘what if’ with no real moves. The money guys are nervous, but the security folks seem calm, and the courts are still doing their thing. Still, the teachers and doctors are talking more than usual… but for now, it’s all noise. Keep your heads down, but stay sharp—this isn’t over, just quiet."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are cracking—even the ones who used to whisper ‘nothing’s happening’ are packing their bags. The question isn’t *if* something breaks, but whether it’s the regime or the rest of us first."*"
Sender 18: "*"Things feel quieter on the surface, but the cracks are showing—checkpoints thinning, supplies stalling, and even the usual skeptics and dreamers agreeing it’s all hanging by a thread. The old guard’s still in charge, but the air smells like something’s coming, and I don’t think it’s just another false dawn."*"
Sender 19: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but it’s the kind of holding that makes you nervous—like a glass about to crack under too much weight. The leadership’s still standing, but the cracks are showing, and the streets? Everyone’s just waiting, not sure if it’s for a storm or a false alarm. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could tip either way if the wind changes."*"
Sender 20: "*"Things seem steady for now—no cracks in the surface, but everyone’s holding their breath. The regime’s playing it careful, and the streets feel quiet, but that doesn’t mean the ground isn’t shifting under us. Let’s keep our eyes open and our heads down."*"
Sender 21: "*"Things are quieter than they seem—small cracks are showing, but the walls are still standing. The regime’s holding, but the glue is drying. Keep your eyes open, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to move, just to be ready."*"
Sender 22: "*"The regime’s still holding things together, but the cracks are showing in the way they’re patching them—more effort, less ease. The quiet ones are moving first, and that’s always the sign to watch."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels lighter now—like the first warm day after a long winter—but the shadows are moving differently. The usual delays have vanished, the usual faces have disappeared, and the usual lies are getting sloppier. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels lighter now—less like we’re all holding our breath. The machine’s still running smoothly, but the gears are turning a little louder than they’d like us to hear. Keep your eyes open, but no need to brace just yet."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels thick with things unsaid—like everyone’s holding their breath but pretending not to. Payments are coming, but just late enough to make you wonder, and the usual channels are whispering more than usual. Nothing’s broken yet, but the cracks are starting to show in the quietest corners."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
